name: Serverless: functions and a managed database
summary: Functions behind an HTTP endpoint, DynamoDB for data, SQS for background work and a static front end on a CDN, all defined as code. Pay per request, nothing idle, nothing to patch.

fitsWhen.says: serverless or a big cloud is the plan
traffic is spiky or comes in bursts
idle cost should be near zero
a small team that does not want servers

frontend.why: A static bundle on S3 behind CloudFront.

backend.why: One function per route group; scales to zero and bills per request.

database.why: No connection pool to exhaust from many functions; access patterns designed up front.

queue.why: Background work and retries with a dead-letter queue.

auth.why: Managed user pools; the HTTP API validates tokens before a function runs.

infra.why: Every function, table, queue and permission in code.

ci-cd.why: OIDC to AWS, so no long-lived keys in CI.

observability.why: Traces across the API, functions and queue.

testing.why: Handlers are plain functions tested without AWS.

hosting.why: Lambda, DynamoDB, SQS, S3 and CloudFront.

services.name: site
responsibilities: Static front end served from the CDN

conventions: Handlers stay thin and call pure functions
Every table access pattern is documented beside the key design
Functions are idempotent: SQS delivers at least once

adrs.title: DynamoDB over a relational database
adrs.decision: Data lives in DynamoDB with a single-table design.
adrs.why: Functions scale out without exhausting database connections, and there is nothing to patch.

repos.label: app
repos.layout: Front end, functions and Terraform in one repository
